member.param: A Site<double> containing decimal values for different sites. Each site represents a numeric value that will be converted to its binary representation.
The number of bits in the binary representation for each site. If the binary representation is smaller than , it will be padded with leading zeros (or trailing zeros, depending on ).
A boolean parameter indicating the ordering of the binary bits: - If true, the least significant bit (LSB) comes first. - If false, the most significant bit (MSB) comes first.
member.returns: A Samples<int> where each site contains a binary representation of the decimal value as a sequence of integers (0s and 1s).
member.example:
Given a Site<double> containing: - Site "0" with the value 5.0 - Site "1" with the value 3.0
And = 4: - If is true, the result will be: - Site "0": [1, 0, 1, 0] - Site "1": [1, 1, 0, 0] - If is false, the result will be: - Site "0": [0, 1, 0, 1] - Site "1": [0, 0, 1, 1]
member.remarks: This method assumes that the input decimal values are non-negative and will be rounded to the nearest integer before converting to binary. Ensure that the is appropriately selected to avoid data loss when encoding large decimal values.

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.HardIP.CalcFunctionAMP.Calc_AMP_Linearity(System.Int32,System.String[])
member.summary: Calculate VDAC all in one, Delta/Diff Alg::Calc_VDAC(ucsdm0_ts3__dout_1+4094+1.32[+0.66][:storeName],...); optional for delta calc and store
member.remarks:
Alg::Linearity_Calc(CH0_DQ0_code#_test_pol@_ro_count_out_ucs_1,0,95) Alg::Linearity_Calc(CH0_CA_code#_test_pol@_ro_count_out_ucs_1,0,47)
Function: Linearity_Calc Pattern: cz_ptra1_s_fulp_an_ddio_mea_jtg_lp5_mdx00X_si_ucsdm_mdXpi Input Paremeters: {DQ{0,1},CA}_code{0..95}_test_pol{0,1}_ro_count_out_ucs_{0,1}
Calculations:
Case1:code{i = 1..15,32..47,64..79}: DNL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{i} = (#code(i)_test_pol0_ro_count_out_ucs_1 - #code(i-1)_test_pol0_ro_count_out_ucs_1)*96/4094 - 1
Case2:code{i = 16..31,48..63,80..95}: DNL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{i} = (#code(i)_test_pol1_ro_count_out_ucs_1 - #code(i-1)_test_pol1_ro_count_out_ucs_1)*96/4094 - 1
Case3:code{i = 0}: DNL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{0} = 0 DNL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{0}_Special= (#code(0)_test_pol0_ro_count_out_ucs_1 - #code(95)_test_pol0_ro_count_out_ucs_1)*96/4094 - 1
For CA Sweep is from 0 to 47, DQ(0,1) from 0 to 95 INL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{i} = DNL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{0} + DNL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{1} + ..+ DNL_{DQ{0,1},CA}_AtCode{i}

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.HardIP.CalcFunctionANPH.Calc_ANPH_rxoffset_fuse_val(System.Int32,System.String[])
member.summary: calculate the code from IO transition voltage convert from delta reference level and LSB_level ArgList: trim_result_pld,power_pin,ANI_VREF,FuseBitSize,FuseStoreName,lsb_resolution ex: PLD_ANPH,VDDIO12_ANP_S2,RD_VREF_ATB1_85,5,ANPH_rx_oc_dq[x]_ppmu_ate,512
member.remarks: 0.get IO pins trim result 1. Take ANI_VREFR value from PP_SPRA1_H_FULP_AN_AN00_MEA_JTG_DIO_ALLFRV_SI_VREFRD_T8 test; 2 Calculate offset OFFSET = "average" - ANI_VREF; OFFSET can be positive or negative; 3. Calculate steps full_scale_code = argv(5) VREF_LSB = 1200mV / full_scale_code VREF_STEPS = '-' offset / VREF_LSB 4. Calculate the fuse values Fuse the amount of vref steps and the corresponding sign (+/-) of offset Fuse is n bits MSB is sign (1 for positive VREF_STEPS and 0 for negative VREF_STEPS) 5 remaining bits correspond to steps of Vref where LSB of fuse = VREF_LSB "e.g. if VREF_STEPS = d'13 --> x1101 [M to L] Add sign to the MSB If VREF_STEPS is positive (OFFSET = 13mV): fuse value is 01101 If VREF_STEPS is negative (OFFSET = -13mV): fuse alue is 11101"

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.HardIP.CalcFunctionHelper.CalculateBTSCoefficient(System.String[],System.String,CoreTestLibrary.HardIP.CoefficientInfo,Teradyne.Igxl.Interfaces.Public.PinSite{System.Double},Teradyne.Igxl.Interfaces.Public.PinSite{System.Double}@)
member.summary:
Use the formula to calculate the coefficient of BTS by site generic data type.
Step 1 a. Convert the 17-bit 2's complement number into a negative number if the MSB is 1. b. Divide the number by 2^16, and the decimal result is "x0a" c. Compute x0 = (x0a - v0) / v1 Step 2 Traditional Calibration a. a0cal = Tcp - a1x0 - a2x0^2 - a3x0^3 b. Tcp, a1, a2, a3 are constant values. Step 3 Advanced Calibration a. b1cal = k0 + k1x0 b. b0cal = Tcp - b1calx0 - a2x0^2 - a3x0^3 c. Tcp, k0, k1, a2, a3 are constant values Step 4 Coefficient Calculations a. c0 = a0cal - a1v0/v1 b. c1 = a1/v1 - 2*a2v0/v1^2 c. c2 = a2/v1^2 - 3*a3v0/v1^3 d. c3 = a3/v1^3 e. c0A = b0cal - b1calv0/v1 f. c1A = b1cal/v1 - 2*a2v0/v1^2

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.HardIP.CalcFunctionMTRnTS.Calc_MetrologyHSCnTS_ADV_Coefficient(System.Int32,System.String[])
member.summary: Calculates the MTRNTS Advanced Coefficients (C0a, C1a, C2a) based on input binary samples.
member.param: An array of strings containing the arguments.
member.remarks:
The description of arguments: argv[0] - The dictionary name of BTS room temp for calculation. argv[1] - The dictionary name of BTS hot temp for calculation. argv[2] - The dictionary name of NTS room temp for calculation. argv[3] - The dictionary name of NTS hot temp for calculation. argv[4] - The dictionary name of NTS C0a for efuse storing. argv[5] - The dictionary name of NTS C1a for efuse storing. argv[6] - The dictionary name of NTS C2a for efuse storing. argv[7] - The dictionary name of BTS average value. (Optional) argv[8] - The category name of NTS CoefficientTable.
The example of argument format: Calc_MetrologyHSCnTS_ADV_Coefficient(hsc_nts_tg00i_temp_bts_ft1, BTS__Tg001_M1_TEMP10, hsc_nts_tg00i_d_0_ft2, hsc_nts_tg00i_d_0_FT1, hsc_nts_tg00i_c0a, hsc_nts_tg00i_c1a, hsc_nts_tg00i_c2a, Hot_Temp_dict, NTS_N3EP)
This method performs the following steps:
Parses input keys from .
Retrieves binary sample data from TestProgramData.JobData.DsscPreProcessJobData.DigSrcSamplesDictionary.
Converts binary inputs to double-precision floating-point values.
Calculates the C1a, C0a, and C2a coefficients using specific formulas.
Logs the calculated coefficients.
Performs test limit checks on the coefficients.
Converts the calculated coefficients back to binary and stores them in the DigSrcSamplesDictionary.

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.HardIP.ResultSimulationConfig.GetSimulationPolynomialCoefficient(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double@,System.Double@)
member.summary:
Get simulation coefficient for Polynomial calculation based on SimulationType
Derive slope and offset coefficient of SimulationPolynomial Formula: y = Slope * x + Offset Input: Target value = Target, Target factor = Factor, Code Width = Code Assume: Input X = Half of Code will get Output Y = Target value Y. Input X = Full code will get Output Y = Target value multiple factor Equation: (1) Target = Slope * (Code / 2) + Offset (2) Target * Factor = Slope * Code + Offset Result: Slope = (2 * (Factor - 1) * Target) / Code Offset = (2 - Factor) * Target

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.InternalControl.GpibController.SetupCoolerAndHeater(System.String,System.Double,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Configures the cooler and heater settings on the GPIB device and waits for a specified duration.
member.param:
A specifying the cooler/heater setting. The format is "M/A +/- ####", where:
M = Manual mode
A = Auto mode
+/- = Indicates heater (+) or cooler (-)
#### = A 4-digit number representing a 0.1% ratio (e.g., 1000 for 100.0%)
Example: "M+1000" for manual mode, heater at 100.0% ratio.
The time in seconds to wait after sending the command, allowing the setting to take effect.
If set to true, the method will perform a serial poll after sending the command and log the received byte response from the device.

member.name: T:CoreTestLibrary.InternalControl.GpibControlMain
member.summary: Provides a main entry point for controlling and interacting with GPIB devices, primarily for testing purposes. This class contains test methods to configure cooler/heater settings and retrieve temperature readings from a GPIB device.

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.InternalControl.GpibControlMain.SetupCoolerAndHeater(System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Configures the cooler and heater settings on the GPIB device based on provided lists of settings and execution times. This method iterates through the settings, applying each one and waiting for the specified duration.
member.param:
A comma-separated string of cooler/heater settings. Each setting follows the format "M/A +/- ####", where:
MManual mode
AAuto mode
+/-Indicates heater (+) or cooler (-)
####A 4-digit number representing a 0.1% ratio (e.g., 1000 for 100.0%)
Example: "M+1000,A-0500" for two settings. Defaults to an empty string if not provided.

A comma-separated string of execution times (in seconds) corresponding to each setting. If empty, default execution times of 0.0 seconds will be used for all settings. If the number of execution times does not match the number of settings, an will be thrown. Defaults to an empty string if not provided.
If set to true, the method will log the serial poll response from the device after each setting command. Defaults to false.
member.exception: Thrown when the number of settings in does not match the number of execution times in (unless is empty).

member.name: M:CoreTestLibrary.InternalControl.GpibControlMain.GetTemperature
member.summary: Retrieves and logs the current temperature from the GPIB device. This method calls the method with logging enabled.

member.name: T:CoreTestLibrary.InternalControl.GpibDevice
member.summary:
Provides an interface for interacting with a GPIB (General Purpose Interface Bus) device. This class encapsulates the low-level communication functionalities, allowing for connection, command sending, data reading, and serial polling.
GPIB is a standardized digital communication interface primarily used for connecting and controlling programmable electronic measuring instruments, test equipment, and computers.
In this context, it is used for communication between the tester and the prober.

member.name: T:CoreTestLibrary.Rtos.RtosMain
member.summary:
This class represents all the high-level RTOS testing functionality.
Requires SPI-ROM to already be programmed and the SPI-ROM relays switched to functional mode.

Boot the DUT and confirm that the DUT is booted.
Setting the boot pins can optionally be from a pattern if is true and is specified. Sets up Protocol Aware (PA) for the UART port to confirm the DUT boots and prints a PASS message.

member.name: M:IgxlWrapper.CoreTestLibrary.InternalControl.GpibControlMain.SetupCoolerAndHeater(System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Configures the cooler and heater settings on the GPIB device based on provided lists of settings and execution times. This method iterates through the settings, applying each one and waiting for the specified duration.
member.param:
A comma-separated string of cooler/heater settings. Each setting follows the format "M/A +/- ####", where:
MManual mode
AAuto mode
+/-Indicates heater (+) or cooler (-)
####A 4-digit number representing a 0.1% ratio (e.g., 1000 for 100.0%) Example: "M+1000,A-0500" for two settings. Defaults to an empty string if not provided.

A comma-separated string of execution times (in seconds) corresponding to each setting. If empty, default execution times of 0.0 seconds will be used for all settings. If the number of execution times does not match the number of settings, an will be thrown. Defaults to an empty string if not provided.
If set to true, the method will log the serial poll response from the device after each setting command. Defaults to false.
member.exception: Thrown when the number of settings in does not match the number of execution times in (unless is empty).

member.name: T:IgxlWrapper.CoreTestLibrary.Rtos.RtosMain
member.summary:
This class represents all the high-level RTOS testing functionality.
Requires SPI-ROM to already be programmed and the SPI-ROM relays switched to functional mode.

Boot the DUT and confirm that the DUT is booted.
Setting the boot pins can optionally be from a pattern if is true and is specified. Sets up Protocol Aware (PA) for the UART port to confirm the DUT boots and prints a PASS message.
member.param: Set to true if specifying a pattern to boot. False uses the pins specified in the configuration. False by default.
The name of the pattern for booting the DUT. Empty string by default.
